transcript.text: "Hey." Greta settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to."
"Tell me more."
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Recently — someone tripped over nothing and we all lost it. It felt like stealing."
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it. That's the truth of it."
"Yeah?"
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah?"
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"Still on the last time you laughed. — ask anyone!"
"Yeah?"
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"I count. Someone has to."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"Yeah?"
"I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach."
"Yeah?"
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"Yes."
They nod. "Okay."
"Yeah?"
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
(listen)
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
(listen)

"Wait — what were we talking about?"
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah?"
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Yeah?"
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
